title: Deterministic Fallback Orchestration and Capacity Provisioning Blueprint
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary:

This page defines the Deterministic Fallback Orchestration (DFO) pattern and the complementary Capacity Escrow & Broker (CEB) automation used by Redwood Inference to protect SLOs, manage error budgets, and execute predictable capacity changes during reliability events. The blueprint combines SLO-driven decision thresholds, automated model-variant fallback policies, and an escrowed capacity pool to guarantee deterministic degradations with clear ownership and post-incident evidence requirements.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce time-to-mitigation for SLO breaches by automating fallback/routing decisions and provisioning temporary capacity with auditable control.
- Scope: Applies to all model-serving clusters (hosted, dedicated), routing policies, and tenant-tiered traffic. Not a replacement for manual escalations; intended to be the first automatic tier of response for predictable SLO failures.

Key concepts and definitions:
- Deterministic Fallback Orchestration (DFO): A policy engine that selects pre-approved fallback actions (model variant swap, quantized variant, reduced token limit, reject/queue low-priority tokens) based on observed SLO burn patterns. Fallbacks are deterministic: the same trigger set produces the same actions.
- Capacity Escrow: A reserved pool of provisioning capacity (GPU instances / burst slots) kept for emergency allocation. Escrow capacity is tracked separately from normal autoscale pools and can be leased via the Capacity Broker.
- Capacity Broker: A small control-plane service (internal service name: rwd-capacity-broker) responsible for validating escrow requests, allocating capacity, and tracking escrow leases with TTL and reason codes.
- Error budget burn signal: Normalized burn rate computed per rolling window (typically 5m, 30m, 3h) used to decide when to trigger DFO.

SLO and trigger examples (production defaults):
- Generation API (public-hosted): Availability SLO = 99.95% monthly; Latency SLO = p95 < 200ms, p99 < 500ms (for short prompts < 512 tokens). Error budget window: 30 days.
- Embeddings API: Availability SLO = 99.9%; Latency SLO = p95 < 120ms, p99 < 300ms.

Automated trigger thresholds (recommended):
- Alert: Error budget burn_rate_5m > 2.0 -> page SRE on-call (alert: SLO-BURN-5m).
- Escalation: burn_rate_30m > 1.5 AND burn_rate_5m > 1.0 -> start DFO candidate evaluation (alert: SLO-BURN-30m).
- Auto-fallback: burn_rate_30m > 3.0 OR sustained p99 latency breach for 15m -> execute DFO fallback actions (policy: dfo-auto-exec).

DFO policy components (policy file fragment):
- id: dfo-priority-1
- conditions: ["p99_latency > 500ms for 15m", "error_budget_burn_30m > 3.0"]
- actions (ordered):
  1. route: reduce-demo-tenant-qps by 50% (token priority low)
  2. swap-model: model: "gptx-8q-int8" -> fallback_variant: "gptx-8q-4bit" (quantized variant)
  3. reduce-max-tokens: global max_tokens -> 512 for non-enterprise customers
  4. capacity-broker-request: pool: escrow, min_gpus: 2, ttl: 30m, reason_code: "dfo-auto-1"

Example policy JSON (stored in config repo):
{
  "policy_id": "dfo-priority-1",
  "conditions": {"p99_latency_ms": 500, "window_m": 15, "burn_rate_30m": 3.0},
  "actions": ["route:reduce_low_priority_qps=50%","swap_model:gptx-8q->gptx-8q-4bit","set:max_tokens=512","broker:escrow:2:30m"]
}

Capacity Escrow & Broker (CEB) mechanics:
- Escrow pool sizing: Recommended baseline = (peak_30d_qps * 0.01) expressed as GPU-minutes. For example, a service with 10k peak qps and avg request cost of 0.05 GPU-seconds => baseline escrow = 10k * 0.01 * 0.05 * 60 = 300 GPU-minutes (~5 GPU-hours).
- Lease lifecycle: request -> validated -> allocated -> leased (TTL) -> returned -> audit record closed. Broker enforces per-tenant and per-team quota against escrow.
- Approvals: automatic for SRE-runbook triggers; manual approval required for cross-tenant escalations when reason_code contains "manual-approval-required".

CLI examples (for on-call SRE):
- Request escrow (automatic path): rwdctl capacity broker request --pool escrow --min-gpus 2 --ttl 30m --reason "dfo-auto-1"
- Force return escrow: rwdctl capacity broker return --lease-id lease-12345 --force
- Inspect leases: rwdctl capacity broker list --active

Operational dashboards and alerts (naming conventions):
- Dashboards:
  - SRE / SLO / DFO Overview (grafana id: dfo-overview) — shows per-SLO burn rates, active fallbacks, escrow consumption, and top affected tenants.
  - Capacity Broker Audit (grafana id: capacity-broker-audit) — timestamps of allocation/return, TTL expirations, owner.
- Alerts:
  - SLO-BURN-5m (PagerDuty): threshold burn_rate_5m > 2.0
  - DFO-AUTO-EXEC (PagerDuty critical): when dfo-auto-exec policy fires and actions changed routing or model variants
  - ESCROW-THRESHOLD-WARNING (Slack): escrow_pool_utilization > 75%

Runbook: Automated detection -> containment -> remediation -> verification -> handoff
1) Detection (SRE on-call receives SLO-BURN-5m alert):
   - Validate alert: check grafana, traces, and a synthetic canary (canary name: dfo-synthetics-short-prompt).
   - Confirm whether latency increases are global or tenant-specific (topk by tenant).
2) Containment (if trigger qualifies for DFO automated flow):
   - Observe if DFO policy has evaluated: rwdctl dfo policy status --policy dfo-priority-1
   - If DFO flagged but not executed, runbook owner (SRE on-call) may trigger with: rwdctl dfo policy execute --policy dfo-priority-1 --dry-run=false --reason "oncall-verify"
3) Remediation (automated action path):
   - If broker requested escrow: validate leases in capacity-broker-audit dashboard and confirm allocation.
   - Confirm routing changes: check topology service (topo) and verify route table entries for low-priority lanes.
   - Verify model swap health: call health endpoint for fallback variant: curl -s -X GET https://internal-model-health/gptx-8q-4bit/health
4) Verification:
   - Run synthetic request load to replicate reduced-latency answer times (synthetic CLI example: rwd-synth run --suite dfo-synth-short --qps 50 --duration 5m).
   - Observe p95/p99 and error budget burn in grafana. If SLOs trending back within tolerance, mark remediation successful.
5) Handoff and post-incident tasks:
   - If remediation required long-running escrow or depended on infra changes, create ticket in SRE backlog and assign to platform-capacity.
   - Required post-incident items (see "Incident review standards" below).

Incident review standards (evidence checklist):
- Timeline: ordered events with UTC timestamps (DS to collect from alerting, DFO audit log, broker audit).
- Trigger artifacts: DFO policy evaluation log, policy input metrics, and exact action list executed.
- Capacity evidence: broker lease id, allocation runtime, host ids, GPU IDs, and the TTL.
- Customer impact table: per-tenant affected percentage, estimated dropped QPS, estimated cost due to fallbacks.
- Root cause analysis: concrete chain-of-events and suggestions for permanent remediation (e.g., model kernel optimization, improved quantization, or capacity increase).
- Lessons learned and actions: action owner, priority, and expected completion date.

Capacity planning & runway guidance (practical steps):
1) Quarterly capacity review: compute 99th percentile production QPS and growth rate. Reserve escrow proportional to expected quarterly spike exposure (recommended: 1–5% of peek GPU-minutes).
2) Runway calc (example):
   - Baseline 99th qps = 12,000 requests/min; avg cost = 0.04 GPU-sec/request -> required GPU-min/minute footprint = 12,000 * 0.04 / 60 = 8 GPUs.
   - Peak headroom target = 20% -> 9.6 -> round to 10 GPUs.
   - Escrow baseline = 2 GPUs for 1 hour = 120 GPU-minutes (safety cushion for 60–120 minutes).
3) Contracting policy: ensure Dedicated and Private contracts expose burst-credits API for ephemeral escrow consumption. Update procurement/finance playbook to treat escrow as operational buffer.

Reliability initiatives & Ongoing improvements:
- Annual DFO policy audit: each policy reviewed for effectiveness and false positives with owners annotated.
- Synthetic house-cleaning: maintain a suite of short, medium, long prompt synthetics that exercise model kernels under quantized and standard variants.
- Telemetry drift detection: automated checks that validate metric definitions (p95/p99) against telemetry schema; failing checks open tickets in telemetry backlog.

Operational tooling recommendations and ownership:
- rwd-dfo-service: maintainers: eng-serving-runtime (primary), eng-sre (secondary).
- rwd-capacity-broker: maintainers: eng-sre (primary), eng-infra (secondary).
- Telemetry: metric owners must maintain an alert playbook; metric names: slo.<service>.<slo_name>.(p95|p99|burn_rate)

Governance and safety controls:
- Determinism requirement: every DFO policy must be deterministic given the same metrics snapshot and must support a dry-run mode.
- Audit trail: all automatic actions must emit an audit event with correlation_id and lease_id where applicable. Audit events are retained for 90 days by default.
- Tenant protection: no automated action will evict enterprise-tier tenants without manual approval (policy flag: protect_enterprise = true).

Change management and rollout guidance for DFO policies:
- Stage: dev -> staging -> canary (1% traffic) -> prod (gradual ramp). Canary runbook must include synthetic validation and rollback criteria (rollback if synthetic p99 increases > 10% vs baseline).
- CI checks: policy linting, deterministic-evaluation unit tests, and simulated metric replay tests.

Appendix: example audit record (CSV friendly):
- timestamp_utc, correlation_id, policy_id, trigger_metrics_snapshot, actions_executed, lease_id, owner, notes
- 2026-02-25T14:31:00Z, cid-78a3, dfo-priority-1, {p99:820, burn_30m:3.6}, [route:reduce_qps50, swap_model:gptx-8q->gptx-8q-4bit, broker:req:2], lease-77, oncall-sre1, "auto-triggered"

Required next steps for adoption:
- Run a 4-week pilot on one high-traffic service (recommendation: embeddings pipeline) and collect false-positive rate, mean-time-to-remediate, and escrow utilization metrics.
- Create a policy registry entry for each service with owner contact, rollback plan, and synthetic test case.
